fields.features_heading: What a Meal Train Settles Before Night One
fields.features_subheading: A meal train sign up sheet shows who cooks each night. This one also keeps the address private and puts the food notes first.
fields.feature_1:
One meal per date, then the date closes

Each date takes one dinner. When a cook claims Tuesday it leaves the list, and the next friend sees only the nights still open, with the drop-off window printed beside each one.
fields.feature_2:
The address goes only to signed-up cooks

The family's street address stays off the shared sheet. A cook sees it in the confirmation email after claiming a date, with notes such as the gate code or the cooler on the porch.
fields.feature_3:
An email reminder the afternoon before

Every cook gets an email the afternoon before their date with the address, the drop-off window, and the family's food notes. Nobody has to dig back through a group text for them.
fields.feature_4:
The week's dishes, shown before cooks pick

Cooks see what the others are bringing that week before they choose. Someone planning baked ziti for Thursday spots Monday's lasagna on the list and switches to chicken soup.
fields.feature_5:
Food notes every cook confirms

Allergies, dislikes, and the number of people eating sit above the dates. Each cook ticks a box saying they read the notes, then lists the main ingredients in their dish.
fields.feature_6:
The whole sheet in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the sheet yourself. A church or school can keep it running for the next family that needs dinners.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Meal Trains Kept Dinner Coming
fields.tab_content_1:
Into the porch cooler by 6 pm, no knocking

Twins came home to the Gildersleeve house, and a neighbor set up 14 nights of dinners. Every date asks cooks to leave the meal in the porch cooler between 5 and 6 pm, while the twins nap, and not to knock. Wilfreda Crowhurst claims night 6 and gets her reminder email the afternoon before.
fields.tab_content_2:
Twelve dinners after knee surgery, no two alike

Jorunn Mirabeau had her knee replaced, and her book club brings dinner every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday for 4 weeks, 12 dinners in all. Each cook sees what is already coming that week before picking a dish. Lysander Brockwell planned lasagna for Friday, saw it on Monday, and switched to white bean soup.
fields.tab_content_3:
Ten days of meals, every gap caught 2 days out

Brierfield Chapel's care team covers 10 days of dinners for a family after a funeral. Any date still open 2 days out sends an email to care-team lead Augustina Hartsfeld. Thursday has no cook on Tuesday morning. She calls two members who cook in big batches, and one of them takes the night.
fields.tab_content_4:
Allergy box ticked by every cook who signs up

Peanuts and tree nuts stay out of the Lowenhart house because their son is allergic to both. The note sits above every date, and a cook claims a night only after ticking a box that says they read it. Philomena Tremayne takes Saturday and lists chicken, rice, carrots, and sesame oil for her stir-fry.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Meal Train Sign-Up Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a meal train sign up sheet that covers every night the family needs, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the length before the dates
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set one drop-off window and place
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep the address for cooks only
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask one person close to the family how many people eat at home and what foods they avoid. Then ask when a drop-off will not wake a baby or a patient. Their answers go above the dates, where every cook reads them before claiming a night.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide how long the meal train runs before you open it. Start with two weeks for a new baby or a short recovery, because adding dates later is easier than canceling cooks. Choose between every night and three nights a week.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give every date the same drop-off window, such as 5 to 6 pm, and one place to leave food. A cooler on the porch lets a tired family skip the door. Say on the sheet whether they want a knock or a text.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Leave the street address off the shared sheet. Have the app email it to each cook after they claim a date, with any gate code or parking note. Anyone who only browses the open dates never sees where the family lives.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask every cook to name the dish
fields.howto_step_5_des: Have each cook name their dish when they claim a night, and show that list to the next cook. Add a short ingredients field for any household with an allergy. The family can check it before the meal reaches the door.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add reminders and a gap alert
fields.howto_step_6_des: Schedule each cook's reminder for the day before their night. Then pick a point, such as 2 days out, when an unclaimed date emails you. Two days leaves time to call a friend or order takeout for the family.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Claim a date with your own email before you share the link. Check that the confirmation shows the address and that your date closes on the sheet. Then post the link in the group chat or the church bulletin.

faq_plan.q: What is a meal train sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: A meal train sign up sheet is a shared schedule where friends and neighbors each claim a date to bring dinner to a family going through a hard stretch, such as a new baby or a surgery. Each entry shows who is cooking and what they will bring. The family's food notes and drop-off instructions sit above the dates.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a meal train sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Describe the sheet in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder: how many dates, the drop-off window, the family's food notes, and who should get reminders. Emergent builds the sheet with its database, and you change any part of it by prompting again. Share the link once a test sign-up works.

faq_plan.q: How long should a meal train sign up sheet run?
faq_plan.a: Plan two weeks to start, then extend it if the family still needs help. Twins or a hard recovery can justify a month. Adding dates to a running sheet is easier than asking cooks to drop out.

faq_plan.q: What should a meal train sign up sheet ask each cook?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the cook's name, email, and phone number, the date they claim, and the dish they plan to bring. Add an ingredients field when the family has an allergy, plus a choice between hot and ready-to-reheat. Keep it under six questions.

faq_plan.q: Can a meal train sign up sheet include takeout or grocery gift cards?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each date a choice between a home-cooked meal, takeout delivered in the drop-off window, and a grocery gift card. Friends who live out of town can still take a night. The sheet Emergent builds has no response caps, however many people sign up.

faq_plan.q: How many meals a week should a meal train sign up sheet cover?
faq_plan.a: Ask the family, since the answer depends on who is eating. Three dinners a week leaves room for leftovers on the nights between. A household with a newborn and older children may want every night for the first two weeks, then three a week after that.

faq_plan.q: What should a meal train sign up sheet tell cooks about containers?
faq_plan.a: Ask cooks to bring food in containers the family keeps or throws away, such as foil pans or deli tubs. A family recovering from surgery or a loss should not have to track and return a dozen dishes. Put the request in the drop-off note above the dates.

faq_plan.q: How do I share a meal train sign up sheet with a group?
faq_plan.a: Post the link where the group already talks, such as a group text or the church bulletin. Share it again a week in, naming the dates still empty. The claims sit in a database you own, and a filter for empty dates shows what is left.

faq_plan.q: Can two people manage the same meal train sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give a co-organizer access to the same dashboard and have the open-date email go to both of you. Split the follow-up by week: one of you covers gaps in the first week, the other in the second.

faq_plan.q: Does it cost money to set up a meal train sign up sheet?
faq_plan.a: It depends on the tool you pick. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing the sheet. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository.

plan.angle: The top 10 for meal train sign up sheet is printable grids on Etsy and Pinterest, a Facebook group post and form templates: a list of dates with a blank for a name. This page shows the sheet as a working schedule for the four situations that start meal trains: a new-baby train with a porch cooler and a quiet drop-off window, a surgery recovery that runs three nights a week, a church care team covering a family after a death, and a household that needs every cook to read an allergy note first. The how-to and FAQ add what printables skip: how long to run it, keeping the address private, avoiding three lasagnas, reminders, and gift-card days.
